title: Ten Winters and One Short Lantern
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）　|　核心词汇：eve　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 eve 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1931 my grandmother ① spent an eve that no neighbour in the town would have named, and she said the spending was the whole of the winter. The ② eve, meaning the night itself and not the day, ran ten winters and stayed unnamed in the book; an eve, she said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ eve in that town had the same short lantern beside it, and the ④ eve at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An eve, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my grandmother said the naming is the part that fills ten winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the eve was the whole of the year, meaning the moment before and not the night. The ⑥ eve, meaning the moment and not any of that, is the only thing in a year that everybody waits for and nobody names; eve, he said, is either something you spend or the only word that means both a night and a moment. He said the moment is the part they remember.

By 1939 the ⑦ eve had become a line in a calendar, and the calendar had become an argument about the short lantern. The ⑧ eve of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one town and ten winters of naming; eve, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ eve I remember is the one named in the calendar, which closed in 1942 and is still described as the quietest in the town. An ⑩ eve, my mother said in 1944, is the only one that improves by being named; every eve, she said, is a moment that has agreed to look like a night. She said the moment was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 前夕；前夜（指镇上每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 前夜（指那一夜本身，与节日当天相对）
C. 固定搭配：spend an eve 度过一个前夜
D. n. 前夜（指留给孩子的那一个）
E. n. 前夜（抽象总称，指一个镇子上的守夜之事）
F. n. 前夜（指年历上写到、被标名的那一个）
G. n. 前夕；紧要关头（指一年里人人都等却无人命名的那样时刻）
H. n. 前夕（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人命名的那种时刻）

items.q: spent an eve that no neighbour in the town would have named
The eve, meaning the night itself and not the day
the eve at the far side

answers.why: spend an eve 意为“度过一个前夜”，1931 年祖母度过了一个镇上没有一位邻居肯命名的前夜。
eve 意为“前夜”，指那一夜本身而不是节日当天，它经过了十个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
eve 意为“前夜”，指镇上每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一盏短短的灯笼。
eve 意为“前夜”，指留给孩子的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
eve 意为“前夕、紧要关头”，指一年里人人都等却无人命名的那样时刻，叔叔说这个时刻就是那一年的全部。
eve 意为“前夕”，指人人都等却无人命名的那种时刻而不是那一夜，是一年里人人都等、却无人命名的东西。
eve 意为“前夜”，指年历上写到、被标名的那一个，到 1939 年这一个成了年历里的一行。
eve 意为“前夜”，祖母一月写道，整件事的守夜之事是一个镇子和十个冬天的命名。
eve 意为“前夜”，我记得的是年历上标名的那一个，1942 年结束了，至今仍被说成镇上最安静的一个。
eve 为抽象总称，母亲 1944 年说，一个前夜是唯一会因为被好好命名而变得更好的东西。
